stem: An investor holds a preferred share paying a perpetual quarterly dividend of Rs 750. At issue the required annual return is 10% compounded quarterly. Rates then shift and the required annual return rises to 12% compounded quarterly. By how much does the share's intrinsic value fall (in Rs) due to this rate change?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Annualises the payment (750 * 4 = 3000) but uses the full annual rate without converting: 3000/0.10 = 30,000 and 3000/0.12 = 25,000, giving the right fall of 5,000 - but student who uses 2% and 2.4% per quarter (tenth of annual): PV_old = 750/0.02 = 37,500; PV_new = 750/0.024 = 31,250; fall = 6,250, then halves assuming semi-annual = 3,125, rounds to 2,500 via confusion.

Uses annual payment 3000 directly with annual rate 10% and 12%, but then applies the difference in PV factors: 3000*(1/0.10 - 1/0.12) = 3000*(10 - 8.33) = 3000*1.667 = 5000; student makes error using 1/0.08 instead of 1/0.12 giving 3000*(10-12.5) = -7500, then takes absolute value 7,500.
Computes PV_old = 750/0.025 = 30,000 correctly but uses r_new = 0.0286 (1/35) instead of 0.03, giving PV_new = 26,250 (approx), so fall = 3,750 scaled to 5,250 via doubling error.

explanation: Perpetuity value is C/r where r must match the payment frequency. When the rate rises, PV falls; the decline equals the difference of the two perpetuity values.

explanation_sections.punchline: Two-rate perpetuity: compute PV_old = C/r_old and PV_new = C/r_new using the per-quarter rate, then subtract.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula PV = C/r, r = per-period rate. C = 750 quarterly. r_old = 10%/4 = 0.025; PV_old = 30,000. r_new = 12%/4 = 0.03; PV_new = 25,000. Decline = 5,000.
explanation_sections.lesson: Perpetuity PV is inversely proportional to the discount rate. A 2 percentage point rise in annual rate (10% to 12%) on a quarterly perpetuity drops value by C*(1/r_old - 1/r_new).
explanation_sections.timing: 60-70 seconds. Trap: using 10% and 12% directly instead of 2.5% and 3%. Also watch whether the question asks for fall (positive number = correct) or new value.
